nonvacuity: This is an unconditional assertion about six explicit atoms: masses 1/4,1/4,1/8,1/8,1/8,1/8. Both assignment and receipt arms have mass 1/2, the compliance probability and first stage are 1/2, and the Wald denominators are nonzero. Independent exact-rational checks confirm the law, full-pair independence, receipt means and Wald values (scratch/arithmetic_check.py).

Both incomparability laws have the six positive atom masses of T1. For the general implication, take Omega=Bool with its uniform probability measure, X=Unit, Z=id, and the constant response D0=false,D1=true,Y0=0,Y1=1. Profile probability and compliance are one; both receipt arms have probability 1/2; receipt mean equality holds and the first stage is one. These premises are checked in scratch/Nonvacuity.lean. The extra no-defiers/relevance clauses are consequences of the canonical premises, as explained in REPORT.md.

Both 32-atom constructions have strictly positive masses summing to one. All covariate cells have positive mass, and compliance probabilities are (2/5,2/3) or (1/4,3/4). Assignment is an independent fair coin. The inverse-score first stages are 8/17 and 3/8. Exact-rational checks confirm full-type marginal/conditional independence and its failure where asserted, profile effects, arm differences and Wald values (scratch/arithmetic_check.py).

Use the compiled uniform-Bool, all-complier, constant-response model from scratch/Nonvacuity.lean, X=Unit and w=2. It satisfies full IV, positive profile compliance, positive weights and both joint-independence alternatives; the weighted first stage is one. The two retained counterexample laws also have positive masses and nonzero first stages. Finite X makes the relevant weight and profile functions bounded, so all integrals and inverse-score ratios are legitimate.

The defined design has 500 actual rows, 250 assignments in each arm, interior covariate support values and all-complier latent indices 2,-2. Both specified outcome inputs are points in the canonical design's support. The exact Gram matrix, determinant 3906250000 and outcome cross-products are independently checked in scratch/arithmetic_check.py. Positive-weight premises have the instance w=1; full column rank makes every positive-weight Gram matrix invertible.

Positive sample and replicate counts include n=R=1. The benchmark assumptions are realized by the coordinate maps on the finite product of 3n copies of the uniform probability measure on (-1,1). For the expected-error identities, t=B=5 on a one-point probability space satisfies every L2 and mean premise; C=univ realizes the conditional constant-effect claim. T5's explicit inputs give both discrepancy signs. No integrability of Y0 is needed when the actual integrand is the constant (Y0+5)-Y0=5.

For the general positive-log/minimizer assertions, take one observation, Theta=Bool, likelihoods L(false)=1/4,L(true)=1/2, and weight 2; a minimizer exists at true. For the extended zero-weight case take two observations with L=1/2 and weights 0,1. The explicit 16-record witness uses strictly positive masses and weights; its normalized Wald stages are nonzero. Every t>0 gives positive prescribed scores and a nonempty perturbation model; the exact values are independently checked at positive t instances (scratch/arithmetic_check.py).

A nonempty fitting instance has observations Unit x Bool, cell=first coordinate, receipt=second coordinate, and unit weights: each cell has S=F=1 and optimum 1/2. The positive-total premises are compiled in scratch/Nonvacuity.lean. The three concrete fitting datasets likewise have positive success and failure totals in every cell. Taking constant positive weights supplies the equivalence instance; the numerical Wald statements have nonzero denominators checked by exact arithmetic.

All nine record cells have positive integer sizes and their sum is 18933. Both race groups and both contact groups are nonempty in each completion. Set Y=0 and choose raw codes W for recorded true, O for recorded false and none outside those recorded cells; this satisfies the raw-code compatibility premise. For e=1/2 the recorded assignment pattern has probability (1/2)^18933>0 under independent assignment. Exact counts, cross-products and conditional mean differences are independently checked in scratch/arithmetic_check.py.

For the sign identity take N=2 and C=W=(true,false), so each true count is one and both groups have positive mass; these count bounds are compiled in scratch/Nonvacuity.lean. A nontrivial grouped instance has four records, groups (a,a,b,b), s=(0,1,2,3), A=(0,1,0,0), with the distinguished group a of probability 1/2 and A constant in b. The nine-cell completions have all relevant positive denominators. Both Raleigh arithmetic differences and the completion signs are independently checked in scratch/arithmetic_check.py.

Witness A has positive masses 9/16,3/16,3/16,1/16; witness B has four masses 1/4. Instrument/error variances are respectively (3/16,3/16) and (1/4,5/2), so correlation denominators are strictly positive. Relevance covariances are 3/32 and 1/8. Their structural, exogeneity and endogeneity moments are independently checked with exact rational arithmetic (scratch/arithmetic_check.py).

The two SEM laws are the concrete nondegenerate T11 witnesses. The common-error SEM equations have, for example, I=K=Unit, Q=0,u=0,beta0=0,beta1=1,Y0=0,Y1=1 as a satisfiable instance. The heterogeneous IV witness has four atoms of mass 1/4, D=Z, effects one and two each with mass 1/2, first stage one and covariance 1/4; thus both noninclusion directions use actual laws.

The one-profile IV law has compliance 1/2 and receipt rates 3/4,1/4. The independent receipt pair has four positive masses 3/16,1/16,9/16,3/16 summing to one, and each displayed fit belongs to the explicitly closed triangle. Boundary natural powers are the canonical convention. The five-per-arm binomial product is normalized and has the stated mean and tail probability, checked exactly in scratch/arithmetic_check.py. Every empirical-rate divisor used here is five, and k<=n prevents truncated binomial exponents.
